sam: Quick note — long-context stress (50k token) shows kv-cache RSS creeping over time and a lot of tiny free slots. Allocator stats attached, looks like extreme striping between slab classes.

jordan: Can you paste the allocator histogram & a small heap dump? Is this the 16k-block config or the new stripe allocator?

emily: pasted a trimmed dump from the repro run:
```
slab_class  block_size  alloc_count  free_chunks  fragmented_bytes
64          4096        12000        2400         3.2MB
128         16384       2200         900          14.8MB
256         65536       80           75           44MB
total free holes: 32k (avg hole ~1.1k)
fragmentation_index ~ 0.37
```

liam: That avg hole + big holes in the 64/128 classes screams cross-allocation padding to me. We recently switched default block_size to 16k for throughput; small tensors end up split across blocks and we get a lot of leftover slack.

sam: FWIW the KV entries are long-context KV (kv length grows with token count) so older entries get partially reclaimed but leave trailing fragments.

jordan: Hypothesis: stripe allocator is distributing tiny entries across many 16k pages, leaving ~1k holes that are never coalesced because buddy scopes don't align. Need either smaller block granularity for small objects or a lightweight compaction pass.

emily: Repro command if anyone wants to run locally:
```bash
./runtest --kv-repro --tokens 50000 --alloc-log=alloc.log --kv-block-size=16384
```
Output attached in alloc.log (large).

perf-bot: perf summary (sample run):
- baseline (16k blocks, no compaction): steady RSS +12% over 1h, p50 latency stable
- experiment (4k small-blocks): RSS flat, tokens/sec -6%
- compactor-proto (background compact every 30s): RSS -8% but CPU +4%

liam: Sounds like tradeoff space: smaller block size reduces waste but hurts throughput. Background compaction helps memory but increases CPU. Need a middle ground: adaptive block-sizing + opportunistic compaction for long-lived ranges.

jordan: Another option: prefer allocating small entries into dedicated small-slab pools (fast-path) and have a background migrator that moves contiguous small entries into one slab to free big holes. That migrator can be IO-priority low.

emily: We also saw the allocator's free-list search degenerating — O(n) scans on free-lists with many tiny holes. A simple segregated free-list by sizeclass + bitmap for contiguous-run detection might speed compaction detection.

sam: Can we try two quick experiments this week? 1) force block_size=4096 for kv only (non-default) and run the long-context test. 2) enable a cheap micro-compactor that merges adjacent free chunks but no relocation.

liam: I'll run (1) in my perf sandbox tomorrow. @jordan wanna take (2) — micro-compactor sketch in code is ~60 LOC.

jordan: Yep I can prototype micro-compactor. Plan: scan free-lists to detect > contiguous_count threshold and merge into bigger free-block entry; don't move live objects. Triggers: fragmentation_index > 0.25 and free_holes > 8k.

perf-bot: queued two jobs: job/kv-4096-scan (owner: liam), job/kv-microcompactor-proto (owner: jordan). ETA: 24-48h.

infra-bot: Canary nodes available in ppool-3 for both runs. Schedule with /canary-run job-id.

emily: Add tracing hooks: tag allocations with origin-model-id so we can correlate fragmentation with specific models/load patterns. Also capture kv-entry age to see if long-tail contexts correlate with holes.

sam: Good call. Also add a simple metric: contiguous_free_runs_count and avg_run_length. Would help A/B.

liam: Quick note — if micro-compactor helps but CPU is high, we can throttle compaction during peak qps using workload-aware policy.

jordan: I'll open a tiny PR with proto compactor + unit tests and an opt-in config flag. Leave defaults unchanged.

emily: Thanks — once PR lands, I'll run the long-context with model A and B and post graphs.

sam: Thanks everyone. Owner list: liam (block-size run), jordan (micro-compactor proto), emily (traces + repro graphs). Will reconvene after perf-bot reports. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: job/kv-4096-scan started (run-84).

liam: quick FYI after first 30m: 4096 run reduced fragmentation_index to ~0.12 and RSS stable. Throughput down ~5% p95 unchanged. More data incoming.

jordan: Nice. If numbers hold we can propose hybrid default: small-blocks for kv cache and keep larger blocks for model weights/other heaps.

emily: Logging note: alloc.log files are large, use: `zstd --ultra -22 alloc.log` before uploading to S3.

sam: Awesome. Please drop links to results in this thread so we don't lose context.

liam: link: https://internal.redwood/perf/runs/kv-4096/run-84 (graphs uploaded)

jordan: PR: https://git.internal/rw/runtime/pull/4321 (proto micro-compactor)

emily: Uploaded traced allocations: s3://rw-perf/kv-longcontext/4312345678/allocs.zst

sam: Closing the loop — if we converge on hybrid allocation + optional compaction we should add an ops doc on tuning thresholds for Dedicated customers.

liam: Agreed. I'll draft the doc after we pick defaults.

sam: End of thread for now.
